dag.description: Offline model-comparison / evaluation-only harness: DummyDataLoading loads a fixed comparison dataset -> TabularPreprocessing -> PyTorchModelEval (comparison_mode); DummyTraining injects an already-trained PyTorch model (pretrained_model_path) into the eval, which diffs the model's scores against a previous/production score field. No Package/Payload/Registration.

agent_context.when_to_use: Validate a candidate/locally-trained PyTorch model against a baseline before promotion, e.g. confirm a MODS-migrated model reproduces the incumbent production model's scores (neat_spam_pytorch local-vs-MODS comparison). DummyTraining injects an already-trained model.tar.gz via pretrained_model_path (bring-your-own-model), and PyTorchModelEval runs comparison_mode=true to diff its scores against a previous_score_field on a fixed comparison dataset.
agent_context.when_not_to_use: If you need to train a model (use a training DAG). If you need to package/register/deploy (this DAG intentionally ends at evaluation). If you only want single-model metrics without a baseline comparison (use a standard eval branch).
differentiators: Evaluation-only: no Package/Payload/Registration, terminates at PyTorchModelEval
DummyTraining is a model-injection shim (pretrained_model_path), not a real training step
comparison_mode=true diffs candidate scores against a previous/production score field (previous_score_field)
4 nodes / 3 edges: a data branch and an injected-model branch converge on the eval

prerequisites.check: An already-trained PyTorch model.tar.gz is available
prerequisites.how: DummyTraining.pretrained_model_path points to the model artifact in S3

prerequisites.check: Comparison dataset with the baseline score column
prerequisites.how: DummyDataLoading parquet includes features + the previous/production score field

common_pitfalls: pretrained_model_path must point to a model.tar.gz whose schema matches the comparison dataset's preprocessing
previous_score_field must exist in the loaded dataset for the diff to compute
Large comparison parquets can hit array-size caps; shard the input, and a GPU eval instance speeds up large runs
